entries.title: Trump slaps 50% tariffs on Canada and Carney vows to 'intensify' trade talks
entries.snippet: The duties mark a major escalation in trade tensions between the North American neighbours.

entries.title: Yemen's Houthis announce 'maritime embargo' on Saudi Arabia

entries.title: Rare identical quadruplets born in Australia

entries.snippet: Sixty-seven people have been rescued but the ferry is thought to have had more than 130 people on board.

entries.title: Newcastle, Liverpool and England legend Keegan dies

entries.title: JD Vance says wife Usha and son 'happy and healthy' after birth of fourth child
entries.snippet: The couple welcomed their fourth child, Alec Neel Vance, on Sunday morning.

entries.title: Ryanair profits drop as Iran war puts off passengers and lifts fuel costs
entries.snippet: The Irish airline said oil prices had increased costs meanwhile Brent crude surpassed $90.

entries.title: 'If only people knew what a tick could do' - the deadly meat allergy caused by tick bites
entries.snippet: Mammalian meat allergy is a growing problem along Australia's east coast - and it's caused by tick bites.

entries.title: Norway opens new memorial for victims of 2011 massacre
entries.snippet: The artwork in the capital Oslo was unveiled on Sunday ahead of the 15th anniversary of the attack.

entries.title: Food delivery rider wins China's top literary prize
entries.snippet: Wang Jibing is among blue-collar Chinese workers gaining wider attention for their literary works.

entries.title: FDA still focused on Taylor Farms lettuce as Cyclospora source despite retracted test
entries.snippet: The FDA says lettuce distributed by Taylor Fresh Foods and Taylor Farms de Mexico is still linked to the multistate outbreak of cyclosporiasis. But the source may be difficult to definitively trace.

entries.title: 10 things that wowed us at the 2026 World Cup
entries.snippet: The United States, Mexico, and Canada co-hosted the nearly six-week tournament. NPR's team of journalists who covered the World Cup reflects on the experience.

entries.title: Court ruling freezes Paramount-Warner Bros. merger for now
entries.snippet: Paramount's owners were hoping they'd be firmly in control of rival Warner Bros. Discovery by the end of this week. Monday's temporary restraining order puts that plan on hold.

entries.title: India's Gen Z 'Cockroach People's Party' started as satire but is serious about change
entries.snippet: They call themselves the "cockroaches" and they're on the march — demanding action against corruption, amid a shortage of opportunities for young people in India.

entries.title: Putin meets North Korean foreign minister in diplomatic push
entries.snippet: The visit by North Korean Foreign Minister Choe Son Hui comes without an obvious occasion, such as a multilateral diplomatic event or state anniversary, and has raised speculation that she may be coordinating a possible visit to Russia by North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.

entries.title: 3 U.S. personnel killed in Iran conflict. And, Hunter Biden opens up to NPR
entries.snippet: Three U.S. service members have been killed since Friday amid rising tension between the U.S. and Iran. And, Hunter Biden talks to NPR's Newsmakers about addiction and public scrutiny.

entries.title: At least 930 people have died in Congo's Ebola outbreak
entries.snippet: Congo's health ministry said the deaths were recorded out of the 2,344 cases confirmed as of Saturday. Thirty-seven new deaths were recorded in the previous 24 hours in one of the highest totals.

entries.title: U.S. and Iran launch new strikes after 3 U.S. service members are killed
entries.snippet: The U.S. attacks were the ninth consecutive day of bombing since peace talks between the two countries collapsed in dispute over a memorandum of understanding focused on the Strait of Hormuz.

entries.title: Deloitte-run systems denied Medicaid to disabled people. New laws could make it worse
entries.snippet: Complex computer systems that decide whether people get Medicaid benefits have a history of errors. Now, changes to comply with Trump's tax and domestic policy law are inundating those systems.

entries.title: So distressed you can't think straight? Lower the intensity with these 4 skills
entries.snippet: A clinical psychologist shares effective strategies to quickly de-escalate stress and anxiety. That includes dunking your head into a bowl of ice water to trigger your mammalian dive reflex.

entries.title: Live Results: Arizona midterm primary elections
entries.snippet: Arizona Republicans will choose a nominee in a state primary Tuesday to challenge Democratic Gov. Katie Hobbs in November.

entries.title: Colombia's Petro calls on supporters to defend economic reforms in last presidential speech
entries.snippet: Outgoing Colombian President Gustavo Petro called on his supporters to protect his government's social and economic reforms and resist any efforts by the nation's incoming administration to change labor laws.

entries.title: U.S. Virgin Islands' housing authority accused of corruption as federal funding is suspended
entries.snippet: U.S. Housing Secretary Scott Turner said Monday that nine years after the territory received $1.9 billion in disaster recovery funding, it has spent less than a third of the funds.

entries.title: Trump imposes 50% tariffs on Canadian goods, citing disputes over autos, alcohol and cheese
entries.snippet: The move, announced Monday, could unleash a new wave of economic chaos, with risks of higher inflation and further fraying of relations between two nations that had been closely woven together before Trump's return to the White House.

entries.title: The highlights and controversies of the 2026 World Cup
entries.snippet: There was a hero's welcome for the Spanish soccer team as they arrived in Madrid, where throngs of fans cheered their triumphant World Cup win. Spain's victory ended Argentina and its star Lionel Messi's reign, and caps off a tournament that defied expectations on several fronts.

entries.title: Remembering PBS programming executive Sylvia Bugg
entries.snippet: The PBS family is mourning the passing of one of its own, Sylvia Bugg. Sylvia most recently served as chief programming executive and general manager for general audience programming. She was a dedicated and passionate leader, and a staunch supporter of our team at the News Hour.

entries.title: A wave of student loan borrowers have entered default since pandemic-era protections lapsed
entries.snippet: Today, around 9.5 million people — 1 in 5 federal student loan borrowers — are in default, meaning they are more than nine months behind on their payments.

entries.title: FDA is still focused on lettuce supplier as source of parasite, despite faulty test result
entries.snippet: Federal health officials said Monday they remain focused on lettuce from Taylor Farms as the source of a multistate outbreak of a diarrhea-causing parasite, despite inaccurate test results that the government briefly publicized over the weekend.

entries.title: British prosecutors charge a man with murder in death of former politician Ann Widdecombe
entries.snippet: Joshua Kerry was charged after more than a week in custody on suspicion of murder and acts of terror.

entries.title: 5 dead after group attempted to save a struggling swimmer in an Ohio river
entries.snippet: The tragedy occurred two days after five members of a family were killed in southern Utah after a flash flood swept through canyons during a hiking trip.

entries.title: 'I'm in.' Darline Graham says she will run for a full term in Lindsey Graham's Senate seat
entries.snippet: The entrance of Darline Graham into the Republican scramble to select a new Senate nominee further complicates an already rushed process following Lindsey Graham's death earlier this month.

entries.title: Tropical Storm Bertha forms along U.S. Gulf Coast
entries.snippet: Tropical Storm Bertha has formed in the Gulf of Mexico and is expected. Bertha is the second named storm of the Atlantic hurricane season.

entries.title: A former U.S. Army soldier started fire outside a NYC federal building and fired a pellet gun, FBI says
entries.snippet: Andrew Arrabaca, who was a mechanic on Patriot missile systems, is in custody and has been interviewed, an FBI official said.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Iran war: US launches fresh strikes as Trump vows revenge
entries.snippet: The US has launched strikes on Iran for a 10th consecutive night as both sides vie for control of the Strait of Hormuz. US President Trump has promised revenge over the deaths of fallen American troops. DW has more.

entries.title: Mexican drug lord ‘El Mayo’ sentenced to life without parole in US prison
entries.snippet: Ismael "El Mayo" Zambada, a co-founder of the Sinaloa cartel and one of the world's most notorious drug traffickers, was sentenced to life in a US prison.

entries.title: AliExpress hit with record EU fine
entries.snippet: The Chinese retailer has become the latest major online marketplace to face penalties under the EU’s Digital Services Act.

entries.title: England and Liverpool foortball legend Kevin Keegan dies aged 75
entries.snippet: English former striker and manager Kevin Keegan has passed away at the age of 75 after a battle with cancer. He was a two-time European footballer of the year with Hamburg.

entries.title: Russia says bus strike kills 5 in border region with Ukraine
entries.snippet: The strike comes as Ukraine launched more than hundreds of drones at Moscow after a Russian missile barrage on Kyiv, as President Zelenskyy sought to calm growing tensions over Ukraine’s military leadership.

entries.title: Guterres to visit Cyprus as UN seeks to revive peace talks
entries.snippet: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres will visit Cyprus next week in what is seen as an effort to kickstart the stalled peace process. Why now? What is known about the plan? And what might be different this time round?

entries.title: Why a 90-year-old treaty limits NATO in the Black Sea
entries.snippet: A 90-year-old treaty still shapes the balance of power in the Black Sea. As Ukraine fights on against Russia, can NATO project power into waters it can't enter freely?

entries.title: US ties to Israel rattle rare earth deal in Malaysia
entries.snippet: Malaysia's rare earth refinery in Gebeng is essential to a strategic deal between the Pentagon and Australia's Lynas mining corporation. Now, Malaysian activists are using it as leverage to support Palestinians in Gaza.

entries.title: Spain won the World Cup, but Donald Trump 'cast a shadow'
entries.snippet: Though Donald Trump mostly stayed clear of stadiums, the World Cup may influence the US midterm elections. DW looks at the political implications of "the most successful sporting event maybe in the history of the world."

entries.title: Why Japan's new imperial law keeps women off the throne
entries.snippet: New legislation aims to address the shrinking ranks of Japan's imperial family, while preserving male-only succession despite broad support for a female emperor.

entries.title: Meet Andy Burnham, Britain's prime minister
entries.snippet: Andy Burnham has been sworn in as the successor to British Prime Minister Keir Starmer. The former Manchester mayor has become a leading figure in the Labour Party and one of the UK's most popular politicians.

entries.title: How 'blue dot fever' is affecting concerts
entries.snippet: Live music remains popular, but many concerts are struggling with unsold tickets and cancellations. While superstars fill stadiums, smaller venues and acts are facing a crisis.

entries.title: DRC's neighbors boost preparedness as Ebola cases surge
entries.snippet: Uganda, Rwanda and Zambia are strengthening border screening, disease surveillance and emergency response measures. The growing Ebola outbreak in the DRC is raising concerns about cross-border spread.

entries.title: Germany news: Resistance to Nazi terror commemorated
entries.snippet: Monday marks 82 years since "Operation Valkyrie," the failed attempt on Adolf Hitler's life in 1944. Meanwhile, Foreign Minister Wadephul is heading to Africa on official business.

entries.title: Taking stock of 2026 World Cup: Football's biggest show yet
entries.snippet: A worthy world champion, a call from the US president, security concerns and a few pleasant surprises: The biggest World Cup ever is now over. So what will we remember about the 2026 World Cup?

entries.title: UK: Andy Burnham takes office as seventh PM in 10 years
entries.snippet: After securing the leadership of the ruling Labour Party last week, Burnham has been invited to form a government by King Charles III. He promised both stability and major reforms in his first speech.

entries.title: Guyana: Dozens feared dead after ferry capsizes
entries.snippet: Rescuers have been able to save 67 passengers so far. It is unknown exactly how many people were on board as authorities said the passengers' list is inaccurate.

entries.title: India news: Police fire tear gas at 'Cockroaches' parliament march
entries.snippet: Police had not granted permission for the march organized by India's Cockroach Janta Party movement. The CJP said its leader Abhijeet Dipke had been "picked up" by police but not "detained."

entries.title: Iran war: US conducts strikes for 9th night in a row
entries.snippet: The US launched another wave of attacks against Iran, this time reportedly hitting targets in the northwestern city of Tabriz and elsewhere.
